author: @Vas
source: Original complete relative_arithmetic_group_equiv contract from MazurTheorem Order13IntegralPicardRelativeArithmeticGroupEquivPublic.lean, Apache-2.0, Vas and contributors. The entire original statement is retained, including the exact structural scalar map, canonical relative group-law instance and actual literal function field. The proof now composes the Proved public literal-fibre group compatibility with a Proved public comparison of two Picard representations and the already Proved public existential arithmetic field equivalence. It imports no private arithmetic-constructor cache and supplies no arithmetic dictionary, genus, rank, cardinality or finiteness hypothesis. Reuses original official Anthropic FLT Picard, curve and divisor-class APIs at exact upstream pin 6e837e75355538c7f80bab5b956861e86c4eacc2. The complete original closed kernel type is checked against both the solution and public statement; native, strict and full frontend checks pass with standard axioms only. Named downstream consumers: the same integral family’s rational and mod-3/mod-5 arithmetic groups, torsion specialization and rational rank comparison. The public place-foundation Definition is imported explicitly so that the literal function-field alias in the unchanged statement is visible independently of implementation caches.

This is a derived nonvanishing transfer result, not a claim of the sharp Ramanujan–Petersson bound.

title: Simultaneous defect thresholds from exact source-row counting
author: @yousofy
source: Original research note for yousofy with Codex, 20 October 2026, 'A sharper simultaneous tournament-labeling certificate', sections Exact row count through Five exact certificates. Mathematical proof independently audited; not yet kernel-checked. Let F_q(d)=sum_{a≤q} choose(d,a). For fixed I,c of size t, labels on outgoing rows are independent and the exact probability is 2^{-choose(t,2)} product_i F_q(d_i). The degree sum is choose(t,2). Log-concavity of F_q balances this product: B_q(t)=F_q((t−1)/2)^t for odd t, and (F_q(t/2−1)F_q(t/2))^(t/2) for even t. For cutoffs [24,31,38,44,50], the sum of K^t 2^t B_q(t)/(t! 2^choose(t,2)) is less than 833/1000: individual upper bounds are 60/1000,770/1000,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000. Exact product bases for q=1,2,3,4 are 16,32852,2802228,197839476. A union bound leaves a labeling avoiding all five bad-set sizes. Larger sets restrict to a forbidden cutoff-sized set. The local Python exact-integer certificate and full prose proof are in the accompanying research package. Retains the tournament-labeling provenance of Robin Kothari/Codex, accepted foundation https://prove2.me/theorems/49fdd176-c319-4f1e-b15f-b1fd5130f0bc, and OpenAI's sensitivity construction.

title: Sharper simultaneous defect bounds retaining the zero-defect threshold
author: @yousofy
source: Original note for yousofy with Codex, 20 October 2026, 'A sharper shared-labeling theorem using row counts and the asymmetric local lemma', sections Row count through Exact certificates. Independently audited mathematical proof; Lean proof unfinished. For cutoff t_q, set E_q=choose(t_q,2), a=floor((t_q−1)/2), b=E_q−t_q*a, B_q=F_q(a)^(t_q−b)*F_q(a+1)^b, p_q=2^(t_q−E_q)*B_q. Use activities x_q=p_q*(254/253)^E_q. Exact rational arithmetic gives sum_q choose(12603,t_q−2)*x_q < 1/254. Events depend only on labels of internal arcs; events with disjoint internal arc sets are jointly independent. Cover the neighbors of an event by its E_q internal arcs. For each arc, the sum of neighboring activities is at most S<1/254, so the product of (1−x) over this group exceeds 253/254. Multiplying over arcs gives the asymmetric local-lemma hypothesis. This proves existence of a labeling avoiding every bad cutoff-sized set; restriction rules out larger bad sets. The underlying finite asymmetric LLL is classical: Moser and Tardos, arXiv:0903.0544v3, Theorem 1.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.0544. Exact certificate code: row_labeling_certificate.py, lll_verify(12605,[23,31,38,44,50],Fraction(254,253)). The accompanying full proof records all independence and counting obligations. Retains the accepted tournament foundation attribution https://prove2.me/theorems/49fdd176-c319-4f1e-b15f-b1fd5130f0bc.
